A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Privacy Attacks on Image AutoRegressive Models. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison. Appendices A–K are retained, and v5 adds Appendix L documenting an implementation correction.

before.justification: v4 reports original membership-inference, dataset-inference and training-data-extraction results, alongside ablations, mitigation experiments and memorization analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical studies and reports corrected VAR attack outcomes in the main tables and appendices.

M1.justification: v5 reports a limited correction to VAR inference used by the attack: disabling class-token dropout prevents accidental erasure of the conditional-minus-unconditional membership signal. The attack formula, DI aggregation, extraction procedure and model architectures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet-1k class-conditional evaluations, the captioned-ImageNet VAR-CLIP study, and the same membership-inference, dataset-inference and extraction tasks. No dataset, domain or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same LLM-derived MIA baselines, DM-specific attacks, unified Loss Attack and Maini et al. DI baseline. Changes in scores and the best-performing attack do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Appendix L explicitly reports changing VAR's inference configuration from cond_drop_rate=0.1 to 0.0. This is a reported setting correction, beyond merely disclosing an existing setting. The evaluation splits, 10,000 member and 10,000 non-member samples, metrics and model coverage are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix L adds a focused implementation-error analysis: conditioning dropout reportedly zeroed membership contrasts for approximately 10% of each sample group, and Table 22 summarizes the correction's effects across VAR models. Existing MAR ablations, unified-attack checks, mitigation experiments and memorization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix H retains the statement that results are randomized over 100 experiments and the same plus/minus reporting practice. DI retains Welch's t-test at alpha=0.01. Updated means and uncertainty values do not establish a change in repetition counts or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: The corrected inference setting substantially revises central results. VAR-d30's reported best MIA TPR at 1% FPR changes from 86.38% to 94.57%, and its DI requirement from 6 to 4 samples. Table 16's adapted Min-K% result changes from 1.63% to 93.72% for VAR-d30, while Min-K% replaces Loss as best for the three smaller VARs. Tables 16–17 also revise some MAR/RAR entries.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(9), DI hypotheses and IID assumption, and extraction criteria are retained. Appendix L explains an implementation failure without adding or revising formal theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion revise the headline MIA success from 86.38% to 94.57% and minimum DI requirement from 6 to 4 samples. The central contributions and broader claim of greater observed privacy leakage in IARs than comparable DMs remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1 removes the comparison suggesting VAR-CLIP leakage resembles VAR-d20 and the explanation attributing increased leakage to overfitting richer textual conditioning. Appendix L explicitly withdraws that interpretation following the correction and explains the previous underreporting through zeroed attack signals.

D1.justification: New Appendix L documents the configuration-file change, the VARWrapper override, the February 9, 2026 correction date and source-code locations. These provide concrete reproduction and troubleshooting information absent from v4; existing model, hardware and code-release disclosures remain.

R1.justification: The cited research and positioning relative to prior IAR, LLM and diffusion-model privacy work are retained. The bibliography contains a typographical correction, while the new code-location footnotes document the implementation correction rather than introducing new research positioning.

P1.justification: v5 adds a correction footnote, an acknowledgment and Appendix L with three subsections, removes two interpretive sentences from Appendix B.1, and changes appendix cross-reference wording. The surrounding prose and overall section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v5 adds the two-part before/after Table 22 and updates the plotted VAR results in Figures 1, 2 and 5 while retaining their designs. Table 3 moves from page 7 to page 8, and later memorization figures shift to accommodate Appendix L without changing their content.

improvement.justification: Correcting accidental conditioning dropout makes evaluation more faithful to the stated attack, while Appendix L improves reproducibility and withdraws an interpretation no longer supported by the corrected results. These gains are limited by inconsistent reporting: v5 Table 6 gives VAR-d20's DI requirement as 7 samples, whereas Tables 3 and 22 give 20. Overall, the correction improves validity and transparency within an otherwise largely unchanged study.
